transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, the clinical conversational agent. I've been following up on your cataract surgery recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery that I can help with?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, I'm wondering when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start doing some light gardening, such as brisk walking, gardening, light jogging, and gentle cycling, about 1 week after surgery. Just remember to be gentle and avoid any strenuous activity. Also, don't forget to wear protective eyewear.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you! That's helpful to know. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use your eye drops as prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. And if you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for glaucoma or for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, thanks for clarifying that for me. I'm also finding that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: Yes, it's normal for the eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as it adjusts to the new lenses. If it's mild and just seems brighter than you're used to, wearing sunglasses when you're going outside should help. If you're experiencing significant pain or discomfort, we may need to assess it further.
